request.spec:
A steward can flag a person with a reason and an until date (entries and a button on the row;
PERSON_FLAGGED name=<name> reason=<reason> until=<date>; anyone else or a blank reason is refused
with an error on the row). While the sheet's today is on or before the until date the row shows the
reason, and only a steward may open a claim of that person (alone, by the bulk button, or by a
paste); after the date the flag shows nothing and has no effect.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can flag a person with a reason and an until date (entries and a button on the row;
PERSON_FLAGGED name=<name> reason=<reason> until=<date>; anyone else or a blank reason is refused
with an error on the row). While the sheet's today is on or before the until date the row shows the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The flag feature is in place and its own test (`flags`) passes. The last `bin/e2e` run still fails overall: 2 of the 4 tests pass, and the other 2 fail on behaviour that has nothing to do with flags. I left those two alone because fixing them would mean changing other features.

**What I built**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V99__person_flag.sql`, adds a reason and an until date to each person. Flagging someone doesn't count as an edit of the person, so it can't cause a "someone else changed this person" conflict for another user.
- **Server:**
  - A new `POST …/people/{id}/flag` endpoint. Only a steward can use it, and a blank reason or missing date is refused. On success it writes `PERSON_FLAGGED sheet=… by=… name=… reason=… until=…` to the audit file.
  - People sent to the screen now include the flag reason, but only while the sheet's today is on or before the until date. After that nothing is sent.
- **Opening claims:** while a flag is in force, a claim of that person can't be opened by anyone except a steward. Opening one claim, the bulk open button and paste all go through the same code, so one check covers all three. In a bulk open the blocked claims count as refused and the others still open; in a paste the whole paste is refused.
- **Screen** (`people.ts`): a new Flag column on each person's row with `person-flag-shown`, the `person-flag-reason` and `person-flag-until` entries and the `person-flag` button. A refusal shows the row's existing `person-error`, which clears when either entry is changed.

**Test results**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `flags` (the flag test itself: who may flag, single/bulk/paste opens, expiry, audit lines) | passes |
| `flags scenario 2` | passes |
| `flags scenario 1` | fails at spec line 278 |
| `flags scenario 3` | fails at spec line 1107 |

Neither failing test flags anyone; the only flag check in them is that `person-flag-shown` is empty, and that check passes.
- **Scenario 1:** the audit file expects `PERSON_EDITED … grade=A terms=20` but gets the line without `terms=20`. This comes from how editing a person's terms is logged. A run on the original code, before my changes, failed at exactly the same line.
- **Scenario 3:** with the screen showing the sheet as of 2026-04-02, Ben's due-total shows `n/a` instead of `0.00`. The screen works this figure out from claims and rates, which my change doesn't touch. I couldn't confirm it fails on the original code too, because that run stopped earlier on the then-missing flag column.

I can look into either of those if you want, but each would be a separate fix to existing behaviour.
